therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of autoreactive immune activity and neuroinflammation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with a first demyelinating attack (clinically isolated syndrome) at risk for conversion to clinically definite multiple sclerosis
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Rate of Development of Clinical Definite Multiple Sclerosis (CDMS) Over 10 Years

results.effect_size: 58% cumulative probability of CDMS (immediate) vs 69% (delayed) over 10 years
biomarker_changes: Median new or enlarging MRI T2 lesions over 10 years: 5 (immediate) vs 7 (delayed), p=0.50

context.indication: clinically isolated syndrome / first demyelinating attack at risk for multiple sclerosis
context.comparator: delayed treatment (placebo during original CHAMPS phase III, then interferon beta-1a if converted)
context.investigator_commentary: This is a long-term follow-up study (CHAMPIONS) of the original CHAMPS phase III trial. Immediate treatment with interferon beta-1a was associated with a significantly lower cumulative probability of CDMS (58% vs 69%, p=0.001) and lower annualized relapse rate (0.16 vs 0.33, p=0.02) over 10 years. No significant difference was observed in EDSS >3.5 or MRI T2 lesion counts.
